title: His trumpet style, Red Allen and Sent For You Yesterday
summary: Edison says the solo is his; he admired Red Allen and had no chops for Armstrong's or Eldridge's high playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Was your solo/ "Sent For You Yesterday", wasn't on
Well, your style, how had you developed that style? Because that isn't Louie.
I mean, there's a little bit of Red Allen, I would think.

Oh, he was one of my idols. Oh, yeah, Red Allen was one of my idols because he played in the part of the horn, the register on the horn, that I loved to play in, you see. And then, I think he was sort of the same -- he felt the same way I did, because there's only going to be one Louie Armstrong. And in the first place, I didn't have the chops to play like Louie Armstrong. I didn't have the chops to play like Roy. They are phenomenons, you know. So the lines I played --
(Inaudible) what is your sort of teeth formation? Is that a good --

Oh, yes, but the formation -- I knew some guys that played, they didn't have perfect embouchure but still, they had endurance. But to play high like that, it's a gift. You have to be dedicated to practicing to play higher. So -- and when I was on Jester-Pillar's band, they had more of a smooth band, you had to have tonal quality. You had to really express yourself through playing in a lower part of your horn
